import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Step 1: Join source0 and source2 on 'user_id' to get user gender with ratings
user_ratings = pd.merge(source2, source0[['gender', 'user_id']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the above result with source1 on 'movie_id' to get movie titles
user_ratings_with_title = pd.merge(user_ratings, source1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 3: We now have columns: user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp, gender, title
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'F': float, 'M': float]
# We need to compute average rating per title separated by gender F and M.

# Step 4: Pivot or aggregate ratings by title and gender
# Group by title and gender, calculate mean rating
grouped = user_ratings_with_title.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Step 5: Pivot the gender column to get separate columns for F and M
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating').reset_index()

# Step 6: Rename columns to match target schema
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Step 7: Ensure columns order and types
# Some titles may have ratings only for one gender, fill missing with NaN
pivot = pivot[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Convert ratings to float explicitly (should already be float, but to be safe)
pivot['F'] = pivot['F'].astype(float)
pivot['M'] = pivot['M'].astype(float)

# Step 8: Save the result to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource_cot.csv"
pivot.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2 with Source0 on user_id
df = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source1 on movie_id
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Map gender to columns F and M with ratings
df['F'] = df.apply(lambda row: row['rating'] if row['gender'] == 'F' else None, axis=1)
df['M'] = df.apply(lambda row: row['rating'] if row['gender'] == 'M' else None, axis=1)

# Group by title and aggregate mean of F and M, ignoring None values
result = df.groupby('title').agg({'F': 'mean', 'M': 'mean'}).reset_index()

# Write output with exact target schema and column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
